title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Dipsacus leaf-bearing water retains one explicit bearer across two application sites
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the complete Lonitzer Dipsacus entry, water described as resting on the leaves is said to remedy eye dimness and redness; 'the same water' then removes facial spots. Preserve the leaf-associated water as one explicit material bearer while the recipient/application site and claimed effect change. This is a source content relation, not a Voynich gloss, confirmed recipe, or clinical claim.

whole_source.locator: DIPSACUS entry, VIRES EXTRINSECUS, final two sentences: 'Aqua foliis insidens oculorum caligini et rubedini medetur. Eadem aqua maculas faciei exterit.'
whole_source.layer: CAMENA typed edition of Lonitzer, 1551, as preserved in F_COMPLETE_ENTRIES.md; not a fully corrected diplomatic transcription.

design.content_hypothesis: The source keeps a plant part, its leaf-associated water, and a repeated bearer reference distinct from the two claimed application outcomes: ocular dimness/redness and facial spots. The demonstrative 'eadem aqua' explicitly carries the material across the second operation.
design.contrast: A candidate construction must distinguish material bearer identity from recipient/site identity: one water bearer persists while the application condition changes. It cannot be reduced to an arbitrary plant-name/eye-word gloss or a generic heating permission.
design.smallest_next_authoring_object: If considered later, compare the complete fixed source relation (leaf-associated water -> eye condition; same water -> facial spots) against an already-authorized whole target passage. Require independently fixed material and application-site roles before testing; do not assign any target sign or infer a Voynich water/eye meaning here.
strongest_limits: This is a CAMENA typed edition layer, not a diplomatic correction or independent witness comparison.
The text says water rests on the leaves; it does not explicitly describe deliberate collection, dose, heating, or application technique.
The two effects are historical claims, not present-day clinical evidence.
No target passage, target interpretation, or novelty claim has been established; duplicate retrieval is navigation only.
design.claim_ceiling: One source-grounded RAW_UNREVIEWED proposal. No target meaning selection, experiment, or therapeutic endorsement.
